title: IMPACT and CRASH prognostic models for traumatic brain injury: external validation in a South-American cohort
abstract: Externally validating the IMPACT and CRASH traumatic brain injury prognostic models on an independent low-and-middle-income-country cohort, the authors judged overall model performance adequate, but found calibration disagreements between predicted and observed outcomes. They concluded these models need periodic updating to remain current and generalizable to settings beyond where they were originally developed.

title: Cycle-consistent adversarial networks improves generalizability of radiomics model in grading meningiomas on external validation
abstract: MRI heterogeneity across scanner vendors is identified as a major driver of performance loss when radiomics models are externally validated. This study trained a meningioma-grading radiomic classifier on a single-institution cohort, then used CycleGAN-based image style transfer to reduce cross-scanner heterogeneity before testing on an independent 61-patient external cohort, directly targeting the generalization gap rather than only reporting it.

title: Reclassification of TCGA Diffuse Glioma Profiles Linked to Transcriptomic, Epigenetic, Genomic and Clinical Data, According to the 2021 WHO CNS Tumor Classification
citation: Zakharova et al., International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2022
abstract: Applying the molecular criteria in the 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification, the authors re-derived diagnoses for the public TCGA glioma cohort and found that the majority of cases (828 of 1122) required a changed diagnostic label relative to the earlier 2016 classification, driven mainly by IDH-mutation and related molecular markers. Because most published glioma IDH-status radiogenomic classifiers were trained on ground truth assigned under the older scheme, this reclassification raises the question of how much of a classifier's reported accuracy reflects genuine imaging signal versus label drift between classification eras.

title: Machine-Learning-Based Prediction of Cervical Pedicle Screw Malposition from Clinical and Anatomical Features
abstract: Using 862 cervical pedicle screws from 168 posterior cervical spine surgeries, several machine-learning models were trained on structured clinical and anatomical features to predict postoperative screw malposition. Predictive performance was only moderate across all models (best ROC-AUC 0.69, Balanced Random Forest), which the authors attribute partly to the preoperative imaging- and feature-based predictors being an imperfect proxy for the actual intraoperative and postoperative placement outcome that ultimately defines malposition.

title: Real-World Performance of Large Vessel Occlusion Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer-Aided Triage and Notification Algorithms-What the Stroke Team Needs to Know
abstract: Two FDA-cleared AI tools for detecting large-vessel occlusion on CT angiography were evaluated in real-world deployment at two stroke centers and compared against their manufacturer-reported clearance performance. Sensitivity matched the manufacturer-reported figures when restricted to internal-carotid and M1 vessel segments (about 90.7%), but fell to 76.4% once M2 segments were included and to 59.4% once every proximal vessel segment the devices are meant to flag was considered — a segment-level gap the instructions for use did not disclose.

title: Deep Learning for Outcome Prediction in Neurosurgery: A Systematic Review of Design, Reporting, and Reproducibility
abstract: A systematic review of 35 deep-learning neurosurgical outcome-prediction studies found low adherence to the TRIPOD reporting checklist, with a median of 12 of 22 checklist items left unreported per study. Code was shared in only 3 studies and a final trained model in only 2; no study in the sample described its model as ready for real clinical use — a gap between published performance claims and the reporting rigor needed to assess or reproduce them.

title: Global Disparities in Neuroimaging Research for Mental Health Conditions
abstract: Synthesizing structural MRI data contributed to the ENIGMA Consortium across 83 publications and over 16,000 cases from 27 countries, this study found high-income countries contributed roughly 90% of all cases while low-income countries contributed essentially none, with Africa, South-East Asia, and the Eastern Mediterranean the most severely underrepresented regions — a geographic concentration the authors argue limits how generalizable neuroimaging-derived findings and models are outside a small set of contributing countries.

title: Investigating the methodological foundation of lesion network mapping
citation: Van den Heuvel et al., Nature Neuroscience, 2026 (with subsequent bioRxiv/medRxiv rebuttals)
abstract: This paper argues that lesion network mapping — a technique linking focal brain lesions to normative-connectome-derived networks, foundational to much precision-neurosurgery lesion-symptom research — has a mathematical property causing it to repeatedly sample the same underlying connectivity matrix, so networks reported across very different symptoms end up looking highly similar rather than symptom-specific. The claim was quickly contested by several independent groups, who argue the effect is an artifact of the averaging procedure used rather than a flaw in the method itself — leaving the reliability of a widely used neurosurgical planning tool a live, unresolved dispute rather than settled science as of this notebook's authoring.

title: PitVis-2023 Challenge: Workflow Recognition in videos of Endoscopic Pituitary Surgery
citation: arXiv, 2024 (companion: 'A Guide to Annotation of Neurosurgical Intraoperative Video', ScienceDirect, 2021)
abstract: The PitVis challenge dataset is described by its authors as the first publicly available annotated video dataset of endoscopic transsphenoidal pituitary (skull-base) surgery, assembled from a single academic center's cases. A companion methodological paper on annotating neurosurgical intraoperative video separately notes that, unlike more common laparoscopic and general-surgery video corpora, comparably sized public datasets for skull-base endoscopic procedures remain scarce, constraining the training data available for computer-vision models in this neurosurgical subspecialty.

title: An international study presenting a federated learning AI platform for pediatric brain tumors
abstract: FL-PedBrain is a federated-learning platform coordinating joint tumor classification and segmentation training for pediatric posterior-fossa brain tumors across 19 international sites, built because pediatric brain tumor imaging data remains scarce even at individual tertiary centers. Federated training reached classification and segmentation performance within a few percentage points of pooled centralized training, and meaningfully improved segmentation performance at sites outside the federation's original training network — evidence for federation as a structural response to per-site data scarcity for this tumor class.

title: Quantifying Tertiary Referral Center Bias in Vestibular Schwannoma Research
abstract: Comparing population-based incidence and outcome data against the patient characteristics typically reported in the published vestibular schwannoma literature, this study concludes that most existing research on this neurosurgical tumor is drawn from tertiary referral centers whose patient mix and management patterns differ systematically from the general vestibular schwannoma population — a referral-pathway selection effect the underlying publications do not typically document or correct for.

title: Uncertainty estimation for margin detection in cancer surgery using mass spectrometry
citation: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery, 2022
abstract: Using an intraoperative mass-spectrometry margin-detection tool (iKnife/REIMS) applied during basal cell carcinoma resections, this study adds a Bayesian neural network that produces a real-time confidence estimate alongside each tissue-margin classification, instead of a bare point prediction. Removing samples the model itself flagged as high-uncertainty before retraining improved subsequent performance — illustrating both the value and the current rarity of pairing an intraoperative tissue classifier with a real-time, actionable uncertainty signal for the operating surgeon.

title: Impact of an automated large vessel occlusion detection tool on clinical workflow and patient outcomes
abstract: This study evaluates a deployed automated LVO-detection tool's effect on stroke-triage workflow metrics such as notification and door-to-treatment times. Consistent with a broader pattern in imaging-triage AI evaluation, the evidence reported centers on workflow-timing change, with the paper itself noting that linking these workflow improvements to a measurable improvement in patient outcomes is a separate, and separately difficult, question from showing a workflow metric moved.

title: Machine learning predictive models in neurosurgery: an appraisal based on the TRIPOD guidelines. Systematic review
abstract: This systematic review assessed adherence to the TRIPOD reporting guideline among machine-learning clinical-prediction-model studies published across five major neurosurgery journals between January 2020 and January 2023. Consistent with reporting-quality audits in other surgical and medical-imaging AI subfields, the review documents substantial adherence gaps concentrated specifically in the external-validation and calibration-reporting items, rather than spread uniformly across all checklist items.
